top_signals.title: Democrats Win in Landslide, US Stock Futures Rebound
top_signals.summary:
A Democratic sweep of Congress rippled across global markets, with stocks fluctuating while the dollar fell and Treasuries gained on bets the outcome will put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda.

Futures for the S&P 500 rose 0.2% while those for the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.3%. Both fell earlier before buyers stepped in. The dollar weakened against major peers, while 10-year Treasury yields fell three basis points to 4.93%. Europe’s Stoxx 600 climbed 0.6% and a gauge for Asian equities was little changed.

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Nigeria's Oil and Gas Output Rises to 3.04 Million Boepd
top_signals.summary: Nigeria’s NNPC raised its oil and gas production in September from a month earlier as output was restarted at some oilfields, the state-owned oil and gas company said in its latest monthly report this week. NNPC’s total oil and gas production rose to 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), up from 3.01 million boepd in the previous month, amid slightly higher crude oil and natural gas production and flat condensate output, NNPC’s report showed. top_signals.title: European Bank Stocks Bounce Back as Midterms Ease Uncertainty
top_signals.summary: Bank stocks led European markets higher as a landslide victory for Democrats in the US midterm elections removed some of the uncertainty that has weighed on stocks in recent weeks, while lower bond yields also provided a boost.
